title: PaperAvailability
description: What is known about one paper's text: which identifiers it has and where each came from, what the retrieval waterfall tried, what arrived on disk, and how much of it ASTA's snippet index holds. Written by the `paper-access` CLI and by nothing else — an agent that edits this file is writing an identifier or a title that no API returned, which is the failure mode this record exists to make impossible. A paper reachable only through ASTA is a legitimate outcome with no bytes on disk, so `route` and `local_source` are separate: the first says where the usable content is, the second says what is here.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the record was written against. A consumer that does not recognise it should refuse to read the record rather than guess at missing fields.

input.description: What the caller actually supplied, verbatim — a DOI, a PMID, a PMCID, or a free-text citation. Kept so that a record can be traced back to the line of the input file that produced it, including when resolution turned it into something quite different.

ids.description: The paper's identifiers, each with the provenance of how it got here. An identifier with no provenance entry is not trusted and is rejected by `check`.

route.description: Where this paper's usable content is. 'europepmc' = tagged article XML from Europe PMC's fullTextXML. 'preprint_server' = the JATS a preprint server hosts. 'unpaywall' = an open-access PDF an open-access resolver named. 'manual' = a file a person supplied, taken in by `adopt`. 'asta' = nothing was retrievable, but ASTA's snippet index holds enough of the paper to be queried — there are no bytes on disk and no figure legends. 'none' = no route produced anything; the paper has to be asked for.

local_source.description: The bytes on disk, when there are any. Absent for route 'asta' and route 'none', which is why this is a separate object rather than fields on the record: a consumer that needs a file must test for this rather than for a successful-looking route.

asta.description: What ASTA's snippet index holds for this paper, measured rather than assumed. Present whenever the probe ran, including when a JATS route had already succeeded — the band is a fact about the paper worth recording once, and it is what tells a later multi-paper search which papers it can actually reach.

metadata.description: Basic publication metadata, exactly as an API returned it. Never composed, corrected or completed by a person or an agent: a title that does not match the publisher's is a signal worth keeping.

attempts.description: Every rung the waterfall reached, in order, including rungs that ran and found nothing and rungs that could not run at all. A rung absent from this list was never tried, which is a different claim from a rung that tried and failed.

oa_candidates.description: Every open-access location a resolver named, kept whether or not one was used. Whether a location is the published paper or a preprint of it is a judgement that cannot be made after the fact from a URL alone.

gap.description: What could not be retrieved and what would fix it. Present when route is 'none'.

notes.description: Free text for a human or an agent to record something the CLI cannot know — that a PDF is the accepted manuscript, that the DOI resolves to a correction. The only field outside the CLI's control, and deliberately the only one: it cannot be mistaken for an identifier or for publisher metadata.

fetched_at.description: When the bytes in `local_source` arrived. Absent when there are none.

attempted_at.description: When the waterfall last ran. With `attempts`, this is the negative cache: a paper no route could produce is not re-attempted on every later pass unless a retry is asked for.

Identifiers.description: At least one identifier must be present and confirmed. A record whose only identifier is a candidate has not been resolved and cannot be fetched.

Identifier.description: One identifier and where it came from. The provenance is the whole point: an identifier with `from: input` was supplied by a person, and one with an API name was returned by that API on the recorded date. There is no third way for an identifier to enter this file.

value.description: The identifier, normalised: a DOI lowercased with any `https://doi.org/` prefix stripped, a PMID as bare digits, a PMCID as `PMC` followed by digits.

from.description: 'input' = supplied by the caller and taken as given. Otherwise the API that returned it: 'europepmc', 'idconv' (the NCBI ID converter), 'crossref', 'unpaywall', 'asta'. 'inferred' is deliberately not a value.

at.description: When the API returned it. Absent for `from: input`, which has no lookup behind it.

confirmed.description: False for an identifier proposed by a free-text search and not yet accepted by a person. A record holding only unconfirmed identifiers is a candidate, and `fetch` refuses it.

LocalSource.description: A stored file and what it is. Paths are relative to the directory holding this record, so a store can be moved or shared without rewriting it.

kind.description: 'jats' = tagged article XML, which carries reference markup, document order, and figure and table legends. 'pdf' = a PDF, whose text has to be recovered first and which carries none of those guarantees.

path.description: The stored source, relative to this record.

sha256.description: Digest of the stored bytes, so a later run can tell whether they changed without re-fetching to find out.

url.description: Where the bytes were fetched from. Absent for a manually supplied file, which has no URL.

text_file.description: Text recovered from a PDF, relative to this record. Absent for a JATS source, which is parsed directly.

text_quality.description: What recovering text from the PDF produced. Present whenever `text_file` is, because a PDF that extracts to almost nothing is a scan, and that is indistinguishable from a short paper unless the size is on the record.

AstaIndexing.description: The measured depth of ASTA's snippet index for this paper. Being in Semantic Scholar's metadata graph says nothing about being in the snippet index, and no API field reports coverage — probing is the only instrument. Bands are calibrated on section-name and refMention counts, which separate cleanly and are not finely tuned.

band.description: 'full' = body text indexed; quotable, and reference mentions are positioned. 'partial' = body text present but below the full-text floor. 'abstract_only' = title and abstract only; citation edges may still exist via the graph API but carry no offsets. 'unindexed' = in Semantic Scholar, absent from the snippet index. 'not_in_s2' = no Semantic Scholar record. 'skipped' = the probe could not run, most often no ASTA_API_KEY; nothing was learnt, which is not the same as `unindexed`.

corpus_id.description: Semantic Scholar CorpusId, as `CorpusId:NNNNN`. Absent when the paper is not in Semantic Scholar.

n_sections.description: Distinct section names across the returned snippets. Zero means no body text: one of the two decisive band signals.

n_ref_mentions.description: Reference mentions across the returned snippets. Only a body carries a bibliography, so this is the other decisive signal, and it is orthogonal to the first.

has_figure_legends.description: Always false for content served from ASTA, and recorded rather than left implicit. ASTA's snippets omit figure and table legends, and naming information appears in a legend and nowhere else often enough that a reader of an ASTA-only paper has to know what it is missing.

limit.description: The snippet limit the probe ran at. Counts are not comparable across different limits.

reason.description: Why the band is what it is, in a sentence. Carries the error text for 'skipped' and 'not_in_s2'.

Metadata.description: Publication metadata as one API returned it, kept together with the name of that API rather than merged from several. A blended record cannot be checked against anything.

authors.description: Author names as the API gave them, in order, unparsed.

license.description: The licence the source declares, where it declares one. Absent is common and means unknown, never 'closed'.

source_api.description: Which API produced every field in this block.

Attempt.description: One rung of the waterfall and what it did.

route.description: The rung. 'local' is the cache check that runs first and is not a route: where it succeeds the existing record stands, so a paper supplied by hand last week still reads as supplied. 'asta_probe' always runs and records a band; it becomes the route only when no rung produced bytes and the band is 'full'.

outcome.description: 'ok' = produced what this record carries. 'unavailable' = the rung ran and this paper is not reachable by it. 'failed' = the rung ran and broke, so it is worth retrying. 'skipped' = the rung could not run at all — a missing dependency, no contact address, no API key — and nothing was learnt about the paper.

note.description: What happened, in enough detail to act on.

OaLocation.description: One open-access location as the resolver described it. The resolver's own vocabulary is kept verbatim rather than mapped onto ours, so a value it adds later does not read as invalid.

url_for_pdf.description: A direct link to the PDF where the resolver has one. Frequently absent even for a genuinely open location, leaving only a landing page.

host_type.description: Whose host it is, as the resolver says — typically the publisher or a repository.

version.description: Which version, as the resolver says. A submitted version is the manuscript before review: the science is usually the same but the text is not the published text, so a quote from it may not appear in the article a reader opens.

TextQuality.description: Size and shape of text recovered from a PDF, for judging whether it is worth reading.

mean_chars_per_segment.description: A page of scanned images extracts to a handful of very short segments, which this separates from prose.

sample.description: The opening segments as written, so a reader can see whether they are sentences. Text of the right size that is still gibberish is a real outcome and only the sample shows it.

Gap.description: A paper no route could produce, said in terms a person can act on.

what.description: The paper, named as well as it is known.

action.description: What would fix it: the file to find, where a free copy is if the record found one, and the `adopt` command to run afterwards.
